report:
PASS for the manuscript’s stated partial completion and all-obstacle continuity results. I independently checked all twelve numbered results, their supporting arguments, the native duplicate, and the mathematical source applications. No material defect or unresolved essential dependency remains in this scoped argument. This does not establish the original regularization or contact classification.

The two caller grants remain within their complete clarified scope. A224 supplies only the contextual genuine finite-PA contact obstruction under its disclosed strict-support convention; it supplies neither pair-level regularity nor an operator on the new continuous envelopes. The needed B225 geometry is reconstructed, and the maximum principle is used only after continuous real-endpoint completion. The unindexed task passages below document these grants and are excluded from external-premise coverage.

The cone geometry is sound. At a relative-interior point of τ, the tangent cone consists precisely of affine-hull tangent vectors satisfying the inequalities active on τ. Subtracting points establishes one inclusion for the displayed Cσ/τ; inactive slack establishes the reverse inclusion. Compactness gives uniform positive inactive slack, hence uniform radii and rational generator steps. If there are no inactive constraints, any sufficiently small positive choices suffice. Rational lineality, the bounded pointed section, and active-constraint recursion produce finite rational generators. Eliminating dependent active columns preserves nonnegativity and terminates with an independent subset. Taking inverse bounds over finitely many subsets proves the stated ℓ¹ estimate; rational Gaussian elimination supplies rational coefficients. Representations retain their incident-face assignments.

The inherited star geometry also checks out. Cone faces correspond to original faces containing τ, their tangent spans and saturated lattices agree, and primitive inward normal classes and signs are preserved. Common lineality causes no loss of balancing. The covolume height is aσ/aδ, so the auxiliary Euclidean weights wσaσ give conormal cancellation. Tangential divergence, truncation outside the vector field’s support, and polar integration are valid, including dimension one and cones with lineality. A nonnegative linear form positive somewhere is positive on a positive-measure angular subset of a top cone, contradicting the angular barycenter identity. Independent-column bounds establish closedness of the finitely generated cone; nearest-point separation establishes exact positive spanning. Rational representations of each negative generator yield the strictly positive rational relation. These auxiliary weights never replace raw intersection weights.

Both Jensen combinations are exact. For the upper estimate, A/ε≤1, the coefficients sum to one, and discarding zero a_i terms leaves every endpoint in σ, which contains the center y. The anchor z also lies in σ. For the lower estimate, b_i=(tλ_i−a_i)/ε is nonnegative, the displacement identity is zero, and normalization by 1+Σb_i gives y coefficient 1/(1+Σb_i)>0. Its center is z∈τ, and all endpoint faces contain τ. The bounds Σa_i≤C‖d‖ and Σb_i≤H‖d‖ give the printed constants and transverse estimate. Every endpoint used here is rational.

Automatic rational bounds require no previously assumed bounds on q. A single rational anchor near an arbitrary, possibly irrational, target and its finite generator endpoint values give the upper bound by the upper combination and the lower bound by the reverse combination. Finiteness of the complex excludes nonincident faces from a sufficiently small neighborhood. A zero star is an isolated rational point and is handled without the positive-relation formulas.

The completion argument closes all transverse and shared-face issues. The finitely many translated compact endpoint sets admit finite covers supplying common rational-value bounds. The resulting uniform estimates make rational values Cauchy within each relative face. Comparing arbitrary rational approaches with rational anchors in that face gives the same limit through every incident face. Passing this estimate first to the face limit and then to nearby real points proves continuity in the whole topology. Shrinking rational boxes and their rational triangulations provide genuine PCCs dominating every original irrational value. Thus q≤F; equality away from the rational locus is neither needed nor asserted. The argument permits arbitrary finite downward modifications there, including functions locally unbounded below.

The real-endpoint step preserves the exact face constraints. After discarding zero coefficients, the perspective variables form a rational polyhedron. Its active affine system has rational solutions and a rational affine basis; nearby rational points preserve all inactive inequalities. The retained coefficients stay positive, so division produces rational endpoints in the prescribed faces and rational centers in τ. Continuity then passes the inequalities to the original real PCC. This works on every witnessing rational carrying structure, without discontinuous locality. Domination and rational density establish the exact upper semicontinuous hull, least continuous majorant, uniqueness, and the converse downward-modification assertion.

The fan criterion is sharp at the origin. Rational subdivision handles lineality and makes the origin a vertex without changing support or generated cone. Its sufficiency uses only that star. Separation supplies the stated jump function when the generated cone is proper; its Jensen proof works even with real endpoints. The two-quadrant example satisfies every PCC on arbitrary structures: negative-quadrant centers use the globally minorizing affine function −x; other nonhorizontal centers have value zero; positive horizontal centers force active endpoints onto the horizontal axis, where |x| gives Jensen. Its nonvertex jump therefore correctly prevents the proposed strengthening. This example is outside the balanced domain.

The unrestricted envelope proof is complete for every bounded continuous obstacle and every continuous PC reference. The lower competitor γ+inf u makes the supremum nonempty and finite. Printed Jensen inequalities pass directly to the supremum. Its completion remains below both the continuous obstacle and the global one-sided growth bound, so it is an original competitor; maximality forces equality. Each individual competitor’s own growth constant also passes to its completion. Translation is a bijection between the corresponding competitor sets, giving the stated nonexpansiveness. No positivity-at-infinity assumption is used. Finite products inherit positive balancing componentwise, so nonseparable product obstacles are included for continuity, without a PA or regularization conclusion.

The compact chart extension is valid in its separately named category. Local arguments keep all endpoints inside chart portions. Integral-affine lattice isomorphisms with rational translations identify rational loci, and density makes local completions agree on overlaps. The completed functions satisfy real-endpoint local inequalities. The normalized reverse combination makes a component’s maximum set open; continuity makes it closed. Local polyhedral neighborhoods are locally connected, so components are open, closed, compact, and finite in number. The actual continuous obstacle attains its component minima. Every unrestricted competitor is dominated by its constant completion, while the displayed componentwise constants are admissible and satisfy the global reference bound.

The finite PA and raw assertions retain the finite bounded rational chart-compatible carrying-decomposition hypothesis in both coefficient categories. Common bounded subdivisions have rational vertices; literal affine values there are rational, so the minima are rational. The real category permits real constants. Constant sequences, or the endpoint plus 1/n, provide decreasing uniform regularizations with bounded reference difference. Every linear part of the componentwise constant endpoint vanishes. Its primitive-normal divisor is therefore zero in every chart, these zero cycles glue, and all positive-dimensional iterates vanish without an additional factorial. In dimension zero every PCC stays at one rational point, the endpoint is γ+u, the zero-fold cycle is the given weighted [X], and the contact gap vanishes. The divergence contradiction correctly excludes a compact globally embedded positive-dimensional positive balanced support.

The half-unit gap is exact: rational values approaching an irrational interior point force approximation error at least 1/2, and γ−1/2 realizes it. Consequently the entire printed relative PC class has neither PA density nor equality with either regularizable class. This establishes no endpoint nonregularizability inference.

I opened the literal primary sources and read the complete pertinent units: BMPS definitions, local-star proof, normal-invariance and refinement proofs, regularizable definition/proof, envelope proof, and Theorem 6.4 with its extension/approximation proof units; BBGS Definition 5.1 and complete Lemma 6.1/Theorem 6.2 proofs. The endpoint conventions differ. BMPS’s (1)⇒(2) step invokes continuous extension and PA approximation of arbitrary φ; these applications fail for discontinuous qγ. The manuscript correctly declines that equivalence. Its density obstruction alone does not decide endpoint regularity. [BMPS v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1), [BBGS version of record](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00209-021-02869-6).

Harmless wording clarifications only: decreasing may mean nonincreasing, with strictly decreasing constant additions also available; q* denotes the neighborhood upper semicontinuous hull, including isolated points; the compact finite-carrying hypothesis governs both coefficient branches. These clarify the printed proofs and require no substantial repair. Finite grids, compilation, hashes, and historical execution claims were not used as continuum certification.

The accepted scope is partial all-obstacle CONTINUITY. Uniform global PA approximation in the separately fixed coefficient categories, general regularizable operator domains and continuity, necessary and sufficient raw contact conditions, reference-compatible global realization of local conditions, and the full original structural classifications remain unresolved. No raw MA is assigned to the general continuous envelopes. No polarized non-Archimedean realization, semipositive lift, mass calibration, or global comparison is supplied.

passages.statement: BMPS v1’s embedded balanced category uses finite pure rational complexes, saturated tangent lattices, primitive inward normals, and positive rational top weights.
BMPS v1 PCCs require rational endpoints, real barycentric coefficients, and endpoint faces containing a face containing the center.
BMPS v1 PA functions are continuous, with integral slopes and rational constants; PCreg uses decreasing uniform γ-bounded PAPC approximation.
For balanced d-dimensional X and PA φ, BMPS v1 defines raw MA by recursively computing φ^d·[X], without an additional factorial.
For balanced X, positive-at-infinity PAPC γ, and continuous u, BMPS v1 envelopes impose q≤γ+u and q≤γ+O(1); orthogonality additionally requires regularity.
For balanced X and positive-at-infinity PAPC γ, BMPS v1 Theorem 6.4 asserts equivalence of bounded-PA-obstacle endpoint regularizability, uniform PAPC(X,γ)-density in PC(X,γ), and PC(X,γ)=PCreg(X,γ).
BBGS’s version-of-record Definition 5.1 allows arbitrary real endpoints; Lemma 6.1 and Theorem 6.2 concern balanced open subsets of pure-dimensional Euclidean polyhedral spaces.
